audits.title: AN AUDIT OF PAEDIATRIC VANCOMYCIN DOSING.
audits.standard: New paediatric vancomycin guideline; six standards with 100% target
audits.setting: Paediatric patients, Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Three of six standards met: 100% correct starting dose; 90% of levels taken at correct time; 93% of actions on out-of-range levels correct; only 33% had initial level in range.

audits.other_findings: Two standards could not be assessed (no neonates or renal impairment); authors suggest four times daily dosing or continuous infusion.
audits.citation: Mohsin-Shaikh S, Lumb P. AN AUDIT OF PAEDIATRIC VANCOMYCIN DOSING. Arch Dis Child. 2016;101(9):e2. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2016-311535.10. PMID: 27540188.

audits.title: AN AUDIT OF VANCOMYCIN PLASMA CONCENTRATIONS WHEN VANCOMYCIN IS ADMINISTERED BY CONTINUOUS INTRAVENOUS INFUSION IN NEONATES.
audits.standard: Desired therapeutic vancomycin plasma concentration 15-25 mg/L
audits.setting: Neonatal Intensive Care Unit, Birmingham Women's NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.period: January to July 2014 (intermittent bolus regimen, retrospective)
cycle1.result: 28% of concentrations within the therapeutic range.

audits.intervention: Switch to continuous intravenous infusion regimen (loading dose 15 mg/kg then 20-50 mg/kg/day by creatinine and CGA).

cycle2.result: 62% of 115 concentrations within range (first 60.8%, second 60%, subsequent 65.6%); 71.3% allowing 10% variability.

audits.other_findings: Another hospital using pharmacy-prepared syringes achieved 77%; authors plan prefilled syringes and a re-audit.
audits.citation: Whitticase L, Holder G, Cawsey M, Bedford-Russell A. AN AUDIT OF VANCOMYCIN PLASMA CONCENTRATIONS WHEN VANCOMYCIN IS ADMINISTERED BY CONTINUOUS INTRAVENOUS INFUSION IN NEONATES. Arch Dis Child. 2016;101(9):e2. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2016-311535.56. PMID: 27540238.

audits.title: P02 An audit of vancomycin dosing in the neonatal units

cycle1.result: Correct initial dose 28/28 (100%); level taken at correct time 13/15 (87%); 19/31 levels (62%) within 10–20 mg/L; all 6 levels >20 mg/L had next dose held, but follow-up adjustment often suboptimal; 3 of 4 low levels not acted on.

audits.intervention: Guideline amended (single safe range 10–20 mg/L, doses adjusted on levels not age) and teaching sessions with worked examples planned for prescribers and nurses.
audits.other_findings: 19 patients had 28 courses and 31 levels. Levels appeared to be interpreted in isolation, causing avoidable repeat high levels.
audits.citation: Penny F, Shruti P. P02 An audit of vancomycin dosing in the neonatal units. Archives of Disease in Childhood. 2018;103(2):e1.5-e1. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2017-314584.13.

audits.title: P39 Continuous vancomycin dosing: an audit and evaluation
audits.standard: Local vancomycin prescribing and therapeutic drug monitoring guidance

cycle1.result: Loading, initial continuous dosing and TDM generally in line with local guidelines; 9% of first levels subtherapeutic; of 298 levels 56% therapeutic, 19% supratherapeutic, 25% subtherapeutic

audits.other_findings: A previous audit of intermittent dosing found 50% of first levels subtherapeutic; no vancomycin-specific adverse effects.
audits.citation: Fiona R, Rachel W, Mildrid Y. P39 Continuous vancomycin dosing: an audit and evaluation. Archives of Disease in Childhood. 2018;103(2):e1.43-e1. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2017-314584.48.

audits.title: P003 Intermittent vancomycin in paediatrics: implementation and audit of a new guideline
audits.standard: Trust intermittent IV vancomycin guideline (2016) with loading dose and increased dose and frequency versus BNFC
audits.setting: Paediatric wards (patients ≥1 month) on intermittent IV vancomycin

cycle1.result: Pre-implementation audit: 7% of levels in therapeutic range at 48 hours; lack of support for appropriate dosing and monitoring.

audits.intervention: New trust guideline for intermittent IV vancomycin (loading dose, higher dose and frequency) with pharmacist intervention.

cycle2.result: Loading dose used appropriately in 83%; levels at correct times in 90%; 40% in range at 48 hours; 100% reviewed at 48 hours; out-of-range levels reviewed per guideline in 40%, rising to 80% with pharmacist intervention.

audits.other_findings: 30% still needed dose adjustment at 48 hours. Authors plan for pharmacist prescribers to adjust treatment directly.
audits.citation: Gray J. P003 Intermittent vancomycin in paediatrics: implementation and audit of a new guideline. Archives of Disease in Childhood. 2019;104(7):e2.5-e2. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2019-nppc.13.

audits.title: P15 Two-cycle audit on paediatric vancomycin prescribing and monitoring: tertiary centre experience
audits.standard: Local trust guideline (2018) for intravenous vancomycin in children
audits.setting: Tertiary centre; paediatric patients (>30 days and <17 years) receiving intravenous vancomycin

cycle1.result: Correct frequency 75.9%; correct first dose 58.6%; concentrations taken at correct time 89.7%; therapeutic first concentration 24.1% (70.4% under range); second concentration in range 61.9%.

audits.intervention: Significant changes to electronic prescription and concentration report templates; guideline recirculated to all paediatric prescribers.

cycle2.result: Correct frequency 92.6%; correct first dose 71.4%; concentrations taken at correct time 96.2%; therapeutic first concentration 19.2% (65.4% under range); second concentration in range 57.9%.

audits.other_findings: Non-compliance with prescribing was due to prescribers following BNFC rather than trust guidance. Therapeutic concentrations were still not achieved in over 80% of patients, prompting a call to re-evaluate the dosing guideline.
audits.citation: Chin M, Williams E. P15 Two-cycle audit on paediatric vancomycin prescribing and monitoring: tertiary centre experience. Archives of Disease in Childhood. 2023;108(5):8.2-9. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2023-nppg.14.

audits.title: P14 Improving adherence to and effectiveness of an adult critical care vancomycin continuous infusion protocol: a pilot quality improvement and administration data accuracy project
audits.standard: Local ICU vancomycin continuous infusion protocol; steady-state serum concentration target 20-25 mg/L with daily monitoring

cycle1.result: Per-protocol prescribing/administration of loading and maintenance doses with daily monitoring 39% (7/18); therapeutic concentrations within 48 h 3/9.

audits.intervention: Protocol dosing revised (2 g loading dose for >90 kg, new renal function categories, higher maintenance dose for CLCR >90 mL/min); protocol made accessible via ePMA and CliniBee/Microguide app; protocol teaching added to medical and nursing induction.

cycle2.result: Per-protocol prescribing/administration with daily monitoring 68% (15/22); therapeutic concentrations within 48 h 54% (7/13).

audits.other_findings: Paper drug charts recorded both loading and maintenance doses 38% (5/13) less often than ePMA; administration time differences >60 min in 38% (3/8) of loading and 31% (4/13) of maintenance doses. Staff turnover periods were linked to lower compliance.
audits.citation: . P14 Improving adherence to and effectiveness of an adult critical care vancomycin continuous infusion protocol: a pilot quality improvement and administration data accuracy project. JAC Antimicrob Resist. 2023;5(Suppl 1).

audits.title: Vancomycin use for haemodialysis patients-Development of a new dosing protocol.
audits.setting: Renal service, Waitemata District Health Board, Auckland

cycle1.result: 23% of vancomycin levels within target range (15 treatment courses); 13% of courses had >50% of pre-dialysis levels in range.

audits.intervention: New protocol with weight-based loading dose and dose titration according to same-day pre-dialysis levels.

cycle2.result: 46% of levels within target range; 56% of courses had >50% of pre-dialysis levels in range.

audits.other_findings: Fewer doses were withheld after the protocol; sample too small to interpret clinical outcomes.
audits.citation: Ho E, Gleeson S, Roberts S, Bondesio K, Salmon A. Vancomycin use for haemodialysis patients-Development of a new dosing protocol. Nephrology (Carlton). 2023;28(4):227-233. doi:10.1111/nep.14144. PMID: 36651874.

audits.title: An Audit to Evaluate Vancomycin Therapeutic Drug Monitoring in a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit.
audits.standard: Target vancomycin trough 10-20 mg/L; TDM per protocol
audits.setting: Neonatal intensive care unit, Westmead Hospital

cycle1.result: Target trough reached in 75% of courses after the initial dose and 84% after dose adjustment; appropriate dosing 121/129; TDM correct 51/93.

audits.other_findings: 129 courses in 69 patients; dose adjustment done in 18/29 courses.
audits.citation: Alrahahleh D, Xu S, Zhu Z, Toufaili H, Luig M, Kim HY, et al.. An Audit to Evaluate Vancomycin Therapeutic Drug Monitoring in a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit. Ther Drug Monit. 2022;44(5):651-658. doi:10.1097/ftd.0000000000000986. PMID: 35383737.

audits.title: Vancomycin audit in the paediatric population: Patterns of use and appropriateness of therapeutic drug monitoring.
audits.standard: Prespecified criteria for vancomycin dosing, duration and therapeutic drug monitoring

cycle1.result: Initial doses appropriate in 73.1%; prolonged use (>5 days) in 45.7% of culture-negative admissions; TDM appropriately ordered for 90.7% of concentrations; recorded dosing and sampling times inaccurate in 83.9% and 82.7%

audits.other_findings: Simulation predicted inappropriate dose adjustment in 37.9% of patients because of timing errors; 77.4% of prescriptions were empirical.
audits.citation: Abdel Jalil M, Khaled F, Qaryouti F, Abu Hammour K, Alsous M, Al-Iede M. Vancomycin audit in the paediatric population: Patterns of use and appropriateness of therapeutic drug monitoring. Basic Clin Pharmacol Toxicol. 2023;132(5):425-433. doi:10.1111/bcpt.13849. PMID: 36847106.

audits.title: An audit of the adherence to dosing and therapeutic monitoring of intravenous vancomycin in accordance with the trust’s antimicrobial guidelines
audits.standard: Trust antimicrobial guidelines: seven standards on indication, loading and maintenance dose, trough timing, dose adjustment, missed doses and pharmacist screening
audits.setting: Epsom & St Helier University Hospitals NHS Trust; adult inpatients

cycle1.result: Indication documented 96%; correct loading dose 65.3%; correct maintenance dose 64.7%; initial trough on time 32.23%; subsequent troughs 35%; correct dose adjustments 44%; pharmacist screened 57.33%. No targets met.

audits.intervention: Findings shared, TDM education for junior pharmacists and digital prompts on EPMA.
audits.other_findings: Prospective audit not feasible because of staffing pressures.
audits.citation: Adams O. An audit of the adherence to dosing and therapeutic monitoring of intravenous vancomycin in accordance with the trust’s antimicrobial guidelines. International Journal of Pharmacy Practice. 2024;32(Supplement_2):ii11-ii12. doi:10.1093/ijpp/riae058.012.
